lots.guide_summary: Close entries run from about AUD 104 to AUD 663. Two are SOLD (AUD 104 and AUD 151, both small, lesser sketches with doubtful Invaluable price records). One is UNSOLD (Sworders, bid AUD 265 against an estimate of AUD 473-663). None is ASKING. Category guides outside the range: AUD 28 (a minor sheet) up to AUD 1609 (a large museum-provenance watercolour). Rate GBP 1 = AUD 1.8929 (open.er-api.com, 30 Sep 2026). Invaluable does not say whether priceResult includes premium.
lots.working: No SOLD entry is the same item: this is a unique watercolour, and no sold Harding of similar finish, size and certainty was found in the last 24 months. The two sold comps are small sketches with inconsistent price records, so the rule gives keep_max_hammer 0 and flip_max_hammer 0. For information only: if the attribution is right, the Sworders passing (bid AUD 265) and the Claydon sale (AUD 151) suggest a real UK hammer of about AUD 150-450. If it turns out to be a follower or a later copy, it is a decorative Victorian watercolour worth about AUD 50-150. Buyer's premium at Gowans is 19.8%.
lots.confidence_reason: The signature is only partly legible in a low-resolution crop (reads 'J D Harding 185?', and Gowans says 1854). Nothing supports the attribution beyond the signature and style. No SOLD comp is the same kind of work, and the sold prices come from Invaluable JSON that the lot pages hide and that do not agree with their own bid fields.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: a competent picturesque river scene, with cattle watering at the lower right, a twin-towered red brick Tudor-style house in the middle distance, a warm sunset sky and bodycolour highlights, very much in Harding's manner. Photo 2: dark timber frame with a gilt slip, a wide tan mount and a green inner slip, under glass. Photo 3 (signature crop, enlarged): dark brown lettering in the lower right water reads 'J D Harding 18[5?]', and the final digit disappears under the mount. The strokes look drawn or scratched into the wash and are cruder than the painting itself. That is not proof of a later addition, but it is not reassuring. No visible tears or stains. Paper tone and foxing cannot be judged through the glass.
lots.condition: Appears sound and clean in the photos, framed under glass with a later mount. Paper condition, fading and foxing cannot be checked. The frame and mount look 20th century.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the signature and date written on the sheet itself, and can you confirm the date is 1854? Is the 35 x 51 cm the sight size or the frame size? Are there any labels, gallery stickers or inscriptions on the backboard (Agnew, exhibition, earlier sale)? Any foxing, toning or fading when seen out of the glass?

lots.what_it_is: Pro Hart (1928-2006) hand-coloured etching, pub or cafe scene (woman in yellow, pipe smoker in red shirt, man in purple at the bar, ginger cat, framed picture of a dog on the wall), pencil signed 'Pro Hart' lower right and numbered 14/100 lower left, 15.5 x 20 cm (per Gowans), framed with a black mat.

sold.note: SOLD. same_item: yes. The same image ('Cafe Scene'), hand-coloured etching, ed. 22/100, 15.5 x 19.5 cm, pencil signed. I opened the page ('Sold at Auction', currentBid 200, estimate AUD 250-350, 4 bids) and compared the Lawsons photo with the Gowans photo side by side: same composition and figures, and the hand colouring differs only slightly. Invaluable does not say whether the price includes premium; it is probably hammer.

SOLD. same_item: yes. The same image ('Pub Scene'), hand-coloured etching, ed. 9/100, 15.5 x 19.5 cm, signed lower right and editioned lower left, exactly as ours. Page opened ('Sold at Auction', currentBid 220, estimate AUD 200-300, 13 bids) and photo compared: a match. Premium inclusion unknown.

SOLD. same_item: yes (the same image, titled 'Afternoon Drink', 15.5 x 20 cm, signed, and an A.P. rather than a numbered impression). Gibson's catalogued it as a 'colour lithograph', which is probably a cataloguing difference, but I note it. Page opened ('Sold at Auction', currentBid 140, estimate AUD 100-300, 4 bids) and photo compared: a match. Premium inclusion unknown. The lowest of the three.

SOLD. same_item: category guide (a different image, 'Mineshaft', hand-coloured etching, ed. 8/100, smaller at 10 x 7 cm). Page opened ('Sold at Auction', currentBid 80, estimate AUD 150-250). Shows that the small Pro Hart hand-coloured etchings can sell soft. Not used for the maximum bids.

lots.dropped_entries: The researcher supplied no entries. Not used: other Pro Hart etchings (Bic Man, Work Yard, Camping Scene, The Camp, The Shed, at AUD 90-300 at Lawsons in 2026). They are different images, so I kept only the Mineshaft sale as a category guide.
lots.guide_summary: All three same-image entries are SOLD: AUD 140 (Gibson's, Mar 2026, A.P.), AUD 200 (Lawsons, Dec 2025, 22/100) and AUD 220 (Lawsons, Jan 2026, 9/100). No UNSOLD or ASKING entries. All prices are in AUD, so no conversion was needed. Invaluable does not say whether the prices include buyer's premium. A different small Pro Hart etching made AUD 80 in Sep 2026.
lots.working: keep_max_hammer = lowest same-item SOLD (AUD 140, Gibson's Mar 2026) / 1.198 = 116.86, rounded down to AUD 115 (all-in about AUD 138). If the Gibson's A.P. is set aside, the lowest is AUD 200 / 1.198 = 166.9, or AUD 165, but I have used the conservative figure. flip_max_hammer: likely resale AUD 200 (median of 140, 200 and 220), less about 20% seller's commission and fees when consigned to a Sydney or Melbourne auction room (AUD 40), with no outbound postage because of a drop-off, gives net AUD 160. 160 / 2.396 = 66.8, rounded down to AUD 65. Inbound freight is AUD 0 (pickup at Moonah).
lots.confidence_reason: I read the pencil signature 'Pro Hart' and the edition '14/100' in the photos. Three same-image SOLD results from the last 10 months, all with pages opened and photos compared directly. Remaining risk: that this is a genuine hand-coloured etching rather than a reproduction, which cannot be confirmed from photos.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: the image matches the Lawsons 'Pub Scene' and 'Cafe Scene' and the Gibson's 'Afternoon Drink' exactly (figures, cat, dog picture, window with trees and birds), with loose hand watercolour washes over etched line. Photo 3: pencil signature 'Pro Hart' in the lower right margin. Photo 4: pencil '14/100' in the lower left margin. Photo 2: pale limed timber frame, black mat with a pink slip. The sheet looks clean, with no visible foxing or fading. No plate mark can be seen, because the mat covers the margins.
lots.condition: Looks clean and bright in the photos, with no visible foxing, staining or fading. Framed under glass and matted, so the plate mark and paper edges cannot be seen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you see a plate mark or embossing under the mat, to confirm it is an etching and not a reproduction? Any foxing or fading when out of the frame? Any gallery label or certificate on the back?

lots.working: No same-item SOLD entry exists, because this is a unique watercolour. The only close sale inside 24 months (Claydon, AUD 72, a different subject) gives an indicative figure of 72 / 1.198 = AUD 60. I did not use it as a maximum because the rule needs the same item. On flip: resale of about AUD 70, less fees of about AUD 15-20, divided by 2.396 is about AUD 20. Not worth pursuing, so both maximums are 0.
lots.confidence_reason: The signature 'L. Burleigh Bruhl' reads clearly in photo 3, and the identification as Louis Burleigh Bruhl (1861-1942, President of the British Water Colour Society) is secure. There is only one relevant SOLD result in 24 months, its price comes from Invaluable JSON rather than the visible page, and the other comps are old.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 (enlarged): the signature 'L. Burleigh Bruhl' in dark wash at lower left, fluent and consistent with the painting. Photo 1: a continental canal town with a stone gate tower, an arched bridge, timber buildings, twin Gothic spires and reflections, in a muted palette with a warm sky. Photo 2: olive green mount with a black and gilt inner slip, in a worn moulded frame with some rubbing. The mount looks faded and toned. The sheet looks sound, with no visible tears.
lots.condition: The sheet appears sound. The mount is toned and faded, and the frame is worn at the edges. Any foxing or light-staining of the paper cannot be judged through the glass.
lots.question_for_gowans: Any foxing, fading or water staining to the sheet under the mount? Any label or title on the back?
